quotes.text: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood
and hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father
out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; and hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.
Are not even we laics priests? It is written: A kingdom also, and priests to His God and Father, has He made us.
where three are, a church is, albeit they be laics.
all Christians are truly of the ‘spiritual estate,’ and there is among them no difference at all but that of office
For whoever comes out the water of baptism can boast that he is already consecrated priest, bishop and pope

we are all priests, and there is no difference between us; that is to say, we have the same power in respect to the Word and all the sacraments. However, no one may make use of this power except by the consent of the community
no one can deny that every Christian has God’s Word and is taught of God and anointed by Him to the priesthood.
Such participation by the Christian people as ‘a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a redeemed people’
is their right and duty by reason of their baptism.
The baptized, by regeneration and the anointing of the Holy Spirit, are consecrated as a spiritual house and a holy priesthood
There is nothing higher than this baptismal dignity, equally bestowed upon each person
The gift of the Spirit that every member of the faithful receives in the sacrament of initiation is the charism of royal priesthood.
The first, the basic definition of man is that he is the priest.
The New Testament never uses the term ‘priesthood’ or ‘priest’ (hiereus) to designate the ordained ministry
the term is reserved
for the unique priesthood of Jesus Christ and
for the royal and prophetic priesthood of all baptized.
The clergy are the opposite to the laity. Both these terms are used in Scripture to denote God’s people. Trace them to their origin and we find no difference.
We wish to call christians to consider that Jesus Christ has made them kings and priests to God.
May they not, without a human priest to consecrate the way for them, approach the Lord’s table, and handle the loaf and cup?
where three are, a church is, albeit they be laics.
The apparent question at issue was: may a group of believers not set in order with a presbytery eat the Lord’s Supper or not?
were only two christians in any place, such as on shipboard
they ought to commemorate the death of Christ on the first day of the week
Is there any thing to be done at the table of the Lord, which any brother, who can give thanks for a crucified Savior, and repeat the words of the institution, cannot do?
‘The administration of ordinances’ is a popish phrase, and ought to be cashiered from the christian vocabulary.
He would not tolerate a disciple in his church to baptize a candidate, nor to ‘administer the Lord’s supper,’ nor to pray over the loaf or the cup.
they had appointed two senior members, of a very grave deportment, to preside in their meetings.
he took a small loaf from the table, and in one or two periods gave thanks for it.
each one waiting upon his brother, until all were served.
He may of right preach, baptize, and dispense the supper, as well as pray for all men, when circumstances demand it.

For you cannot find in the New Testament one instance of the church having authority to ordain elders or bishops or deacons, or to administer baptism or the supper. You will find that the ministry existed before the church
they believe that no person but a preacher has a right to administer the ordinances — such as the breaking of the loaf
When he is absent the church can do nothing. Like a widow forlorn and desolate, she is solitary and silent.
One, of course, leads in giving thanks. This is not officiating, for any disciple can do this. It does not pertain to any office.
An ordained minister, as representative of Christ presiding at the Lord’s Table, serves in Christ’s place as host at the Table.
within Australian Churches of Christ ‘lay presidency’ is almost the norm
we have denied women the opportunity to pass Communion trays because we have described it as a ‘leadership role.’
